decisions.reason: Adjusting the framing of the Page 32 photograph does not change any typography rule or resolve the existing bolding ambiguity.
The Page 32 image adjustment is unrelated to the one-page cover letter, signature insertion, or handling of its overflow photographs.
The source changes photograph framing on Page 32, not the background treatment of the specified cover, contents, appendix-divider, or last pages.
The targeted photo-framing revision can be made without changing the current full-document layout coverage, pass count, spacing policy, or general layout approach.
Making the tree more prominent in one photograph does not change the Blue Mesa Strategies identity, logo, or color requirements.
The Page 32 photograph adjustment does not affect inclusion or placement of the organization chart.
The source requests different framing within an existing Page 32 image and does not change the 34-page limit or document-spacing policy.
The photo-framing revision does not alter Canva access, file ownership, editing rights, or asset licensing.
Changing the Page 32 image framing has no necessary effect on the requirement that proposal hyperlinks remain functional.
The Page 32 photograph revision does not change the biography count, affiliation, source, or population method.
The requested photograph framing does not alter the supplied tables, budget sheet, replacement count, or approved table source.
The visual adjustment to one photograph does not change the final PDF format, count, export quality, or email-submission requirements.
